issues.description: Switching to blocking mode loses the timeout and process-exit safety net entirely
issues.detail: Once the first read succeeds, the code drops O_NONBLOCK and enters a blind while-True loop. If the writer wedges after sending one byte, this hangs forever with no poll timeout and no check_process_exited. The whole point of the original poll loop was to detect a stuck or dead subprocess; you just deleted that for everything after byte one.

issues.description: fcntl flag race: another thread or the caller may rely on O_NONBLOCK being set
issues.detail: You mutate the fd's file-status flags mid-function and never restore them. If anyone else holds this fd or reopens it via the same description, behavior changes under them. At minimum, restore the original flags in a finally block. Better: do not flip modes at all, just keep polling with a sane timeout.

issues.description: BlockingIOError branch silently swallowed, removing the prior 'file was closed' signal
issues.detail: The old code treated BlockingIOError-with-content as 'writer closed, we are done.' New code replaces both branches with pass. That may be fine given the new blocking path handles drain, but the has_blocking_error variable and its semantics are now dead. Either delete it completely and explain why, or keep the exit condition.

issues.description: Patch does two things: fixes the race and rewrites the EOF detection path
issues.detail: The bug is 'truncated JSON because we exited before kernel buffers drained.' The minimal fix is: after detecting process exit, do one more blocking drain. Instead this patch restructures the whole loop, deletes the macOS workaround comment, and removes check_process_exited from the hot path. Split it. Bisect-six-months-from-now will thank you.

issues.description: No test reproducing the truncation; correctness argued only in the commit message
issues.detail: The PR description leans hard on a POSIX guarantee. Fine. Then write the test that fails without the patch and passes with it: a subprocess that writes >64KB and exits immediately, run in a loop. Prose is not a regression suite. Without that test this bug returns the next time someone touches this function.

issues.description: Dead comment and dead control flow after the rewrite
issues.detail: The else branch now contains only 'pass' under a multi-line comment about waiting for data. If the branch does nothing, say so in one line or delete it. Leaving stale explanatory comments next to no-op code is how the next reader gets confused about intent.

review.summary: The diagnosis is plausible and the POSIX argument is correct, but the patch is the wrong shape. It fixes the truncation by abandoning the non-blocking poll loop entirely once data arrives, which throws away the subprocess-exit and timeout safety nets that motivated the original design. The minimal fix is: on detected EOF-or-exit, do one final blocking drain — not a permanent mode flip with no restore and no test. NEEDS-WORK: split the patch, add the regression test that reproduces the >64KB truncation, and keep a timeout on the blocking drain.
